    AI Overview
    For the 2026 Masters, golf legends Jack Nicklaus, Gary Player, and Tom Watson served as the honorary starters, teeing off on Thursday morning, April 9, to officially commence the 90th Masters Tournament. This trio, featuring a combined 11 Green Jackets, has led the tradition for the fourth consecutive year. 
    Watch the honorary starters' press conference from the 2026 Masters:
    35:45
    The Masters
    YouTube• Apr 9, 2026
    Key Details About 2026 Honorary Starters 
    • The Trio: Gary Player (3 wins), Jack Nicklaus (6 wins), and Tom Watson (2 wins).
    • Ceremony: The legendary, <>-time Masters champions hit their shots at 7:25 a.m. ET on Thursday morning, with in the as the to mark the Masters as the starters.
    • Action: Gary Player opened, followed by a humorous "Watch out" from Jack Nicklaus, and finally Tom Watson. 
    Masters Honorary Starter Tradition 
    • Origins: The tradition began in 1963, although it was loosely started in 1941 by Jock Hutchison and Fred McLeod, according to and.
    • Legacy: The ceremony serves to honor legends of the game, with only 11 golfers having held the role, including Arnold Palmer, Sam Snead, and Lee Elder.
    • Recent Starters: Following Palmer's last appearance in 2016, Nicklaus (since 2010) and Player (since 2012) were joined by Lee Elder (2021) and later Tom Watson (since 2022).
